column1: # Shared fixture for keys.awk and keys.ps1. One case per line:
# The mode is bash or pwsh. In the command, \n is a newline and \t a tab. The
# expected keys are the extractor's output lines, each written <segment>:<entry>
# and joined with " | ", or "-" for no output. Read by gate-test.sh and
# gate-test.ps1, so a case added here is checked against both extractors.
# Plain commands: the first word, then the subcommand candidates, then the task
# names below each key, which only a PROJECT class reads.

column3: 1:git | 1:git status | 1:git commit | 1:git status commit | 1:+git status | 1:+git commit | 1:+git status commit

1:svn | 1:svn info | 1:svn status | 1:svn commit | 1:svn info status | 1:svn info commit | 1:svn status commit | 1:+svn info | 1:+svn status | 1:+svn commit | 1:+svn info status | 1:+svn info commit | 1:+svn status commit | 1:+svn info status commit
1:gh | 1:gh pr | 1:gh pr create | 1:+gh pr | 1:+gh create | 1:+gh x | 1:+gh y | 1:+gh pr create | 1:+gh pr x | 1:+gh pr y | 1:+gh pr create x | 1:+gh pr create y

column1: # More than 4 candidates at one depth is READ rather than a dropped key.

column2: git -a a -b b -c c -d d -e e x

column1: # More than 8 task names below one key: only a PROJECT key reads the "!".

column2: make a b c d e f g h i
column3: 1:make | 1:make a | 1:make a b | 1:+make ! | 1:+make a b | 1:+make a c | 1:+make a d | 1:+make a e | 1:+make a f | 1:+make a g | 1:+make a h | 1:+make a i | 1:+make a b c | 1:+make a b d | 1:+make a b e | 1:+make a b f | 1:+make a b g | 1:+make a b h | 1:+make a b i

column1: # A word that cannot be read as a name adds the marker "?" at its depth.
# A word directly after a flag may be that flag's value, so it adds the marker
# only when no name follows at that depth, and never among task names.
# Unless no name follows at that depth, when it may be the subcommand itself.
# Wrappers that run the command after them are dropped, with their operand.

column3: 1:hg | 1:hg commit | 1:hg commit x | 1:+hg commit | 1:+hg x | 1:+hg commit x
1:hg | 1:hg commit | 1:hg commit x | 1:+hg commit | 1:+hg x | 1:+hg commit x

column1: # Paths as the first word are keys as written.
# A quoted or odd first word goes to the reader.
# Leading assignments, redirections, shell words, and wrappers are dropped.

column2: FOO=1 sudo -E env BAR=2 nohup git push
if git diff --quiet; then echo same; fi
for f in a b; do rm "$f"; done

column1: # Comments, with a quote in them.
# Separators, and the redirections that are not separators.
# Single-quoted text is skipped when looking for substitutions: a commit
# message's Markdown backticks are not commands.
# A substitution inside double quotes is read (R8).

column3: 1:grep | 1:grep ? | 1:+grep ? | 1:+grep log.txt | 2:gh | 2:gh issue | 2:gh issue comment | 2:+gh issue | 2:+gh comment | 2:+gh x | 2:+gh issue comment | 2:+gh issue x | 2:+gh issue comment x
1:printf | 1:+printf ? | 2:printf | 2:printf x | 2:+printf x | 3:hg | 3:hg commit | 3:hg commit y | 3:+hg commit | 3:+hg y | 3:+hg commit y

1:echo | 1:echo ? | 1:+echo ? | 2:git | 2:git log | 2:git log ? | 2:+git log | 2:+git ? | 2:+git log ? | 3:git | 3:git rev-parse | 3:git rev-parse HEAD | 3:+git rev-parse | 3:+git HEAD | 3:+git rev-parse HEAD
1:echo | 1:echo ? | 1:+echo ? | 2:hg | 2:hg commit | 2:hg commit x | 2:+hg commit | 2:+hg x | 2:+hg commit x

column1: # Pass 1 reads a substitution as the one word "$", so the words after it stay
# with the command around it, and pass 2 reads a process substitution's body.

column2: git diff $(git merge-base a b) HEAD
column3: 1:git | 1:git diff | 1:git diff ? | 1:+git diff | 1:+git ? | 1:+git HEAD | 1:+git diff ? | 1:+git diff HEAD | 2:git | 2:git merge-base | 2:git merge-base a | 2:+git merge-base | 2:+git a | 2:+git b | 2:+git merge-base a | 2:+git merge-base b | 2:+git merge-base a b
1:diff | 1:diff ? | 1:+diff ? | 1:+diff x | 2:gh | 2:gh pr | 2:gh pr view | 2:+gh pr | 2:+gh view | 2:+gh pr view
1:tee | 1:tee ? | 1:+tee ? | 2:hg | 2:hg commit | 2:hg commit x | 2:+hg commit | 2:+hg x | 2:+hg commit x

column1: # Quotes nested inside a substitution inside quotes are misread, toward the reader.
# Heredocs: the body is dropped in both passes.
# An expanding heredoc with a substitution in it is READ (R21-15).
# A sentence in the command adds 0:PROSE: six words or more, the first
# capitalized and the last ending in ".", "!", or "?".

column2: curl -d '{"body":"The report says so and more."}' https://x
python3 -c 'print("Done, all six words are here!")'
python3 -c 'print("the lower case start of this one.")'
echo "The report says so and more.\"
Invoke-RestMethod -Body 'We moved the build to Gradle nine.'

column1: # Body files. With the mode suffix "files", the extractor runs with files=1 and
# prints the operand of each body-file flag in a git commit or a gh pr, issue, or
# release command instead of keys, one line each: 1 when the command may change
# directory first (cd and the like anywhere in it, or git -C), else 0, then the
# operand. An operand of "-" is the command's own stdin and is left out.
# A flag's value is never a flag, even one that reads as -F, and nothing after -- is.
# An operand that is not a literal path is still printed, and the gate reports it.
# gh, per subcommand: -m is --merge in pr merge and --milestone elsewhere, and -p

column2: git commit -F m.txt && gh pr create --title x --body-file pr.md
git commit -F m.txt && git commit --amend -F m.txt

column1: # git and gh read the last body flag. git keeps the "=" of -F=x and takes a
# prefix of --file; gh drops it. git's -S takes only an attached value.
# A letter takes a value in one gh verb and none in another.
# git --work-tree and GIT_WORK_TREE move the directory a relative path resolves in.
# A command that cannot be split has its body files reported as not read, when
# it has a body-file flag at all.
# A sentence in the command adds no line in files mode: the body files are all it prints.

column2: cat >> notes.md <<'EOF'\nThe README now lists the steps for the migration here.\nEOF
gh pr create --title "The README now lists the steps for the migration." -F body.md
Set-Content notes.md 'The README now lists the steps for the migration here.'
